newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler to discuss rural blueprint with ministers over dinner.
newsitem.headline: Fischler to discuss rural blueprint with ministers over dinner.

text.p: Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler will discuss the follow-up to the November Cork Declaration on rural development with farm ministers during an informal dinner on Monday, Commission officials said on Friday.

The declaration, which called for radical reforms to prepare for the next round of world farm subsidy cuts and the EU's expansion east, has run into mounting opposition from Germany, France and other member states, as well as from farmers.

Their concern that Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) funds for farmers will be drained into tourism and other rural economic activities resulted in the Cork Declaration being omitted from the Dublin European Council's conclusions.
"Fischler will look at the next step," a Commission official said.

The official said that many people were confused by the existence of three separate sources of rural development funding -- regional, social and guidance funds -- and that it would be logical to have a single funding programme for each region.
It would also make sense to review rural development funding together with new structural funding guidelines being drawn up for 1999-2005 and with CAP reform, the official added.
Diplomats said that Fischler was being forced to slow down on the Cork Declaration and to seek more reaction from farm ministers.
"It's too important to be rushed or for farm ministers not to be fully consulted," said one diplomat.
